walkthroughs.body_html:
Debates in Contemporary Society (Families & Relationships / Youth / Media) — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Debates in Contemporary Society (Families & Relationships / Youth / Media) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Debates in Contemporary Society (Families & Relationships / Youth / Media).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Parsons identified which two essential family functions?
options: Reproductive and economic
Primary socialisation and stabilisation
Educational and religious
Political and legal

mcqs.q: What is a moral panic according to Cohen?
options: Religious leaders condemning immorality.
Disproportionate media reaction creating exaggerated public concern about a group or behaviour.
Genuine widespread fear about a real, serious threat.
It is treated more harshly than street crime.

mcqs.q: What is Young and Willmott's symmetrical family thesis?
options: The symmetrical family means families with the same number of boys and girls.
It is treated more harshly than street crime.
The symmetrical family means men and women now do exactly equal amounts of housework.
That modern families have moved toward more shared, joint roles between partners — domestic and economic responsibilities increasingly shared, in contrast to segregated traditional roles.
